headline: Mount Sinai researchers found that adding a short safety reminder to an AI prompt cut potentially harmful medical choices from 16.6% to 10.1% across 20 language models.
score_reason: Event is older than 15 Oct (study published 26 Sep, covered 9 Oct); score lowered by 1.
importance_line: Anyone whose care may involve AI tools benefits if simple prompts reduce errors, but about one in ten answers was still potentially harmful, so human review stays essential.
source: Mount Sinai, as reported by Becker's Healthcare
summary: Becker's Healthcare reported on 9 Oct 2026 that researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York found a brief safety reminder lowered potentially harmful choices from 16.6% to 10.1% in a test of 20 large language models on more than 10 million responses; Mount Sinai issued its own announcement on 16 Oct 2026. The study, published on 26 Sep 2026 in Communications Medicine, says the reminder does not replace human oversight.
notes: Mount Sinai page blocked; facts from a Becker's Healthcare excerpt and shattered.io's rewrite of the study. The study itself dates from 26 Sep 2026.
